## Measured boundary

Current tracked files are clean for the measured absolute-home-path, private-IPv4, private-key-header, and common GitHub/AWS/npm token-prefix patterns. GitHub reports zero open secret-scanning alerts.

Reachable history is not clean under the requested publication boundary:

- 137 patch lines contain the current user absolute home path.
- 7 distinct author email identities are reachable; 3 are not GitHub noreply identities.
- 316 commits are reachable.
- No private IPv4, private-key-header, or common token-prefix patch lines were detected by the bounded scans.

No matched private value is reproduced in this issue.

## Required decision and acceptance

Do not rewrite public history without explicit maintainer authorization and a coordinated downstream impact plan. If authorized, preserve an offline recovery bundle, rewrite every affected reachable ref atomically, publish clone-invalidation guidance, and rescan tracked files, packed artifacts, every reachable ref, and author identities before release.

This independently blocks merge/publication even if implementation tests and CI are green.

PM source: [pm-web-priv](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-web/blob/fix/certify-complete-reads-and-refresh-catalog-2026-8-21/.agents/pm/issues/pm-web-priv.toon)

---

### GitHub comments (1)

> **@unbraind** (2026-08-27T04:12:53Z)
>
> ## Decision: freeze the past, gate the future
> 
> Maintainer decision taken 2026-08-27 UTC. **Reachable history will not be rewritten.**
> 
> ### What the measurement actually shows
> 
> - **No keys, tokens, private IPv4 addresses or private-key headers anywhere.** GitHub secret scanning reports zero open alerts, and tracked files are clean — as this issue already recorded.
> - The machine-local commit identities are real but carry no personal data beyond a hostname-shaped address (`bot@unbraind`, `codex@local`, `<redacted-email>`, `<redacted-email>`).
> - `<redacted-email>` is **not** a leak. It is a deliberate public authoring identity, already reaffirmed in an earlier closed decision and allowlisted in `pm-rust`.
> - Every surviving absolute home path is inside `.agents/pm/` prose and history — pm item text, not source, workflows or configuration. Some of it is text that *describes removing host paths*, which reintroduces the string by documenting the fix.
> 
> ### Why not rewrite
> 
> Rewriting reachable history across the fleet would:
> 
> - orphan dozens of release tags,
> - break the provenance chain of already-published npm versions,
> - invalidate every existing clone,
> 
> to remove a Linux username from old commit metadata. That cost exceeds the benefit.
> 
> ### What is being done instead
> 
> A forward gate, added in the release-hardening PR:
> 
> - `.github/approved-git-identities.txt` — the approved author/committer set.
> - `.github/identity-baseline.txt` — the commit from which the gate applies, carrying this decision in prose so it lives where the gate reads it.
> - `test/identity-audit.test.ts` — fails closed on **any** commit after the baseline that carries an unapproved identity, or that adds an absolute home path **in any file, prose included**.
> 
> Verified by violation rather than inspection: an unapproved-identity commit fails it, a commit adding an absolute home path fails it, and a baseline the checkout does not contain fails **all three** tests — so a shallow clone cannot make the gate silently pass, which would be worse than not having it.
> 
> The exposure is therefore frozen at its current size and cannot grow. Closing as decided.
Authorize reachable-history privacy remediation before release
